items.followUp: How does atomic radius generally change down a group and across a period?

rubric.why: Shows the general trend in a group.
rubric.description: Electron affinity generally decreases down a group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it decreases down a group.

rubric.why: Shows the general trend across a period.
rubric.description: Electron affinity generally increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it increases across a period.

modelAnswer: Down a group, electron affinity generally decreases.
Across a period from left to right, electron affinity generally increases.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: Identifies what the donor atom contributes.
rubric.description: A donor atom provides a lone pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the donor provides or donates the electron pair.

rubric.why: Identifies what the acceptor atom does with the pair.
rubric.description: An acceptor atom accepts the lone pair of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the acceptor accepts or receives the electron pair.

modelAnswer: A donor atom provides a lone pair of electrons for bond formation.
An acceptor atom receives that lone pair of electrons.

items.followUp: Define a double covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: States the defining feature of a single covalent bond.
rubric.description: A single covalent bond is formed by sharing one pair of electrons between two atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one pair of electrons is shared.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of a molecule with a single covalent bond.
rubric.description: A correct example is H₂, Cl₂, or HCl.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: A single covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one pair of electrons.
For example, the bond in an H₂ molecule is a single covalent bond.

items.followUp: What is a coordinate covalent bond? Give one example.

rubric.why: Explains that the bond involves a shared electron pair supplied by one atom.
rubric.description: In a coordinate covalent bond, the shared pair is donated by one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the shared pair and its one-atom source.

rubric.why: Distinguishes this bond from ordinary covalent bonding.
rubric.description: Both electrons in the shared pair come from the donor atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one atom contributes both electrons of the shared pair.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent compound contains a bond in which a shared pair of electrons is donated by one atom.
Both electrons in the shared pair come from the donor atom.

items.followUp: Define the boiling point of a substance.

rubric.why: Identifies the temperature at which melting occurs.
rubric.description: Melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the solid-to-liquid change and its temperature.

rubric.why: Specifies that melting point is defined at a stated pressure.
rubric.description: The change occurs at a specified pressure, usually atmospheric pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the specified pressure.

modelAnswer: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid changes into a liquid.
It is measured at a specified pressure, usually atmospheric pressure.

items.followUp: Why does evaporation occur at temperatures below the boiling point?

rubric.why: Explains which molecules leave the liquid during evaporation.
rubric.description: The higher-energy molecules at the surface escape into the air.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that higher-energy surface molecules escape.

rubric.why: Connects the escape of energetic molecules to cooling.
rubric.description: The remaining liquid has lower average kinetic energy, so its temperature falls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the escape of energetic molecules to a fall in the liquid's temperature.

modelAnswer: During evaporation, the higher-energy molecules at the surface escape from the liquid.
The remaining liquid has lower average kinetic energy, so its temperature decreases and it cools.

items.followUp: Classify fog, toothpaste, and sand in water as colloids or suspensions.

rubric.description: Paint, jelly, and milk are colloids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for classifying paint, jelly, and milk as colloids.

rubric.description: Chalk in water is a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chalk in water as a suspension.

modelAnswer: Paint, jelly, and milk are colloids.
Chalk in water is a suspension.

rubric.why: States that the solution contains less than the maximum possible solute.
rubric.description: An unsaturated solution contains less dissolved solute than the maximum amount possible.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains less than the maximum amount of solute.

rubric.why: Recognizes that solubility depends on temperature.
rubric.description: The maximum amount is considered at a given temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying that the comparison is at a given temperature.

modelAnswer: An unsaturated solution contains less dissolved solute than the maximum amount that can dissolve.
This is considered at a given temperature.
